title: Morphisms over an open algebraic space from ideal-power multiples
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $X$ is Noetherian: locally Noetherian on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-locnoeth], quasi-compact, and quasi-separated (its diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests). Modules are sheaves on the small etale ringed site; quasi-coherence is [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and coherent means quasi-coherent with coherent pullbacks on all etale scheme charts [pqf-def-coherent]. For an ideal sheaf $I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ and a module $M$, $I^nM$ is the submodule locally generated by products of $n$ sections of $I$ and one of $M$, with $I^0M=M$. Let $F$ be quasi-coherent, $G$ coherent, and $I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf. Let $U\subseteq X$ be the open subspace where $I$ is the unit ideal; on every affine etale chart it is the complement of the common zero locus of $I$. Restriction induces a bijection $$\varinjlim_{n\geq0}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(I^nG,F)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_U}(G|_U,F|_U),$$ where transition maps are precomposition with $I^{n+1}G\subseteq I^nG$. In particular, for every morphism $u:G|_U\to F|_U$, there exist $n\geq0$ and $\widetilde u:I^nG\to F$ whose restriction, using $(I^nG)|_U=G|_U$, is $u$.

source.place: Tag 07UM, lemma-homs-over-open, first displayed canonical isomorphism and its surjectivity.

proof.text: Choose an affine scheme $W$ and a representable surjective etale map $p:W\to X$, using quasi-compactness. Put $R=W\times_XW$ with projections $s,t:R\to W$. The Noetherian affine-atlas relation lemma says that both $W$ and $R$ are Noetherian schemes and the projections are etale. In particular the overlap need not be affine. For $T=W,R$ write $U_T=T\times_XU$.

source.place: Tag 07UM, lemma-homs-over-open, proof: reduction to the affine etale presentation and its relation, with the final formal descent argument expanded.

proof.text: Restrict the modules to these etale charts. Pullback along an etale map is restriction to the localized site, so local presentations remain local presentations and the restrictions of $F,I$ are quasi-coherent. The hypothesis on $G$ gives coherent scheme modules on both charts. Use the scheme Zariski/etale equivalence to denote the associated Zariski modules by $F_T,G_T,I_T$. The ideal inclusion stays an inclusion. The chart calculus gives quasi-coherence of ideal powers and their products with $G$. To compare products on the two sites, write $I_T^nG_T$ as the image of tensor multiplication: the associated-sheaf functor is exact and is tensor pullback, hence preserves that image and the multiplication map. Iterating from power zero identifies its image with $(I^nG)|_T$. These identifications also preserve the inclusions from power $n+1$ to power $n$. Restriction between etale charts has the same property directly: membership is locally a finite sum of products of ideal sections and module sections, and the coverings in a localized site are precisely the same coverings. Thus $U_T$ is exactly the complement of $V(I_T)$, and on $U$ all the inclusions $I^nG\subseteq G$ are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 07UM, lemma-homs-over-open, proof: reduction to the affine etale presentation and its relation, with the final formal descent argument expanded.

proof.text: For each $n$ let $A_n=\operatorname{Hom}_X(I^nG,F)$, regarded as a $\mathbf Z$-module. Restriction to $U$, using the preceding identification, gives $r_n:A_n\to\operatorname{Hom}_U(G|_U,F|_U)$. Precomposing with $I^{n+1}G\subseteq I^nG$ does not change this restriction, so the $r_n$ form a cocone and induce the asserted canonical map $r$ from the colimit over the small directed poset $\mathbb N$.

source.place: Tag 07UM, lemma-homs-over-open, proof: reduction to the affine etale presentation and its relation, with the final formal descent argument expanded.

proof.text: Given $u:G|_U\to F|_U$, restrict it to $U_W$. Apply the scheme Hom-over-open theorem on the Noetherian scheme $W$, with quasi-coherent $F_W,I_W$ and coherent $G_W$. Its surjectivity gives an integer $a$ and $v:I_W^aG_W\to F_W$ restricting to $u|_{U_W}$. On $R$ the two pullbacks of $v$, identified with maps from $I_R^aG_R$ to $F_R$ by the canonical pullback data, have equal restrictions to $U_R$: both are the pullback of $u$. Apply injectivity of the same scheme theorem on the Noetherian scheme $R$. The difference of these two maps represents zero in $\varinjlim_n\operatorname{Hom}_R(I_R^nG_R,F_R)$. The elementwise filtered-module-colimit criterion gives $b\geq a$ at which the difference is zero. Replace $v$ by its precomposition with $I_W^bG_W\subseteq I_W^aG_W$. Its two pullbacks to $R$ now agree as actual maps, and its restriction to $U_W$ is still $u|_{U_W}$.

source.place: Tag 07UM, lemma-homs-over-open, proof: reduction to the affine etale presentation and its relation, with the final formal descent argument expanded.

proof.text: By the quasi-coherent groupoid equivalence for the atlas $W\to X$, the map of the preceding step, which commutes with the two canonical pullback data on $R$, descends uniquely to $\widetilde u:I^bG\to F$. This equivalence applies because both its source and target are quasi-coherent, as checked in step 2. Its restriction to $U$ equals $u$: for any etale scheme test $T\to U$, the map $T\times_XW\to T$ is a surjective etale cover and the two morphisms have equal components there. The separatedness part of the sheaf axiom for $F|_U$ gives equality of their components on $T$. This proves surjectivity of $r$ and the stated extension clause.

source.place: Tag 07UM, lemma-homs-over-open, proof: reduction to the affine etale presentation and its relation, with the final formal descent argument expanded.

proof.text: To prove injectivity, take a colimit class whose image under $r$ is zero. The filtered-module-colimit representative criterion writes it as a map $v:I^aG\to F$. Its pullback to $W$ restricts to zero on $U_W$. Injectivity of the scheme theorem on $W$, followed by the eventual-zero criterion for filtered module colimits, gives $b\geq a$ such that $v|_W$ vanishes on $I_W^bG_W$. The map $v\circ(I^bG\hookrightarrow I^aG)$ therefore pulls back to zero on $W$ and is zero on $X$ by faithfulness of the quasi-coherent groupoid equivalence. Our class is zero. Thus the canonical group homomorphism $r$ has trivial kernel and is surjective, hence is the claimed bijection.

lean.statement: theorem coherent_homs_over_open {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hln : ∀ T : X.EtaleSite, IsLocallyNoetherian (X.etaleForget.obj T)) (hqc : CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj)) (hqs : ∀ (V W : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ X.obj.obj) (b : yoneda.obj W ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsAffine V.left → IsAffine W.left → CompactSpace (Point (Limits.pullback a b))) (F G I : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) (hGqc : G.IsQuasicoherent) (hGcoh : ∀ T : X.EtaleSite, RingedSpace.IsCoherent (X.etaleForget.obj T).toRingedSpace ((X.schemeRestriction T).obj G)) (i : I ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit X.structureSheaf) [Mono i] (hI : I.IsQuasicoherent) : ∃ (U : AlgebraicSpace S) (j : U ⟶ X) (hj : IsEtale j.hom.hom), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ q ↦ IsOpenImmersion q.left) j.hom.hom ∧ (∀ T : X.EtaleSite, (∃ a : yoneda.obj T.obj.left ⟶ U.obj.obj, a ≫ j.hom.hom = T.obj.hom) ↔ Function.Surjective (i.val.app (op T))) ∧ ∃ (P : ℕ → X.Modules) (p : ∀ n : ℕ, P n ⟶ G), (∀ n : ℕ, Mono (p n)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (T : X.EtaleSite), Set.range ((p n).val.app (op T)) = idealPowerSubsheafSections i G (fun _ ↦ Set.univ) n T) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, IsIso ((pullback j hj).map (p n))) ∧ ∃ r : ∀ (n m : ℕ), n ≤ m → (P m ⟶ P n), (∀ (n m : ℕ) (h : n ≤ m), r n m h ≫ p n = p m) ∧ (∃ (D : ℕ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}) (e : ∀ n : ℕ, D.obj n ≅ AddCommGrpCat.of (P n ⟶ F)) (c : D ⟶ (Functor.const ℕ).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of ((pullback j hj).obj G ⟶ (pullback j hj).obj F))), (∀ (n m : ℕ) (h : n ≤ m) (χ : P n ⟶ F), (e m).hom (D.map (homOfLE h) ((e n).inv χ)) = r n m h ≫ χ) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (χ : P n ⟶ F), (pullback j hj).map (p n) ≫ c.app n ((e n).inv χ) = (pullback j hj).map χ) ∧ Function.Bijective (colimit.desc D ⟨_, c⟩)) ∧ ∀ ψ : (pullback j hj).obj G ⟶ (pullback j hj).obj F, ∃ (n : ℕ) (χ : P n ⟶ F), (pullback j hj).map (p n) ≫ ψ = (pullback j hj).map χ
